subtitle: Song, Siege, and the Orphaned Hills

panels.shot: wide low-angle of Kapilar and Vel Pari standing on a misty hill, distant armies faint on the horizon
panels.action: Kapilar of Parambu stands beside Vel Pari atop a rugged hill of Parambu Nadu, winds tugging their hair and cloaks as terraced slopes and faint campfires of distant kings dot the valleys below under a brooding sky.

dialogue.text: In the remembered hills of Parambu, poet Kapilar sings of Vel Pari, and words stand watch where spears close in.

i18n.hi: परंबु की यादों वाली पहाड़ियों में कापिलर कवि वेल पारी गाते हैं, शब्द पहरा देते हैं, भाले घिर आते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in from bird's-eye over Tamilakam to mid-shot of Kapilar in a crowded court
panels.action: A sweeping view of ancient Tamilakam’s landscapes fades into an indoor court where Kapilar sits cross-legged among other bards, palm-leaf manuscripts at his side, as a minor chieftain listens on a carved wooden dais.

dialogue.text: In the age remembered as Sangam, poets moved between courts, singing of love, war, hills and seas, and winning their bread with measured lines.

i18n.hi: संगम के दौर में कवि दरबार दरबार घूमते थे, प्रेम, युद्ध, पहाड़, सागर गाते, और छंदों से रोटी कमाते।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Kapilar reciting, listeners in soft blur behind him
panels.action: Kapilar leans forward, eyes alight, hands gently shaping the rhythm as he recites, a circle of listeners—warriors, merchants, women—watching him in a smoky hall lit by oil lamps.

dialogue.text: Tradition gives Kapilar many songs. The colophons remember him as a master of the mountain land, where mist and stone weigh on the heart.

i18n.hi: परंपरा कापिलर को कई गीत देती है; प्राचीन टीकाएँ उन्हें पहाड़ों के कवि कहती हैं, जहाँ धुंध और पत्थर मन पर भारी हैं।

panels.shot: transition shot from a generic court dissolving into the high hills of Parambu
panels.action: The scene shifts from the court to a rugged mountain pass, with Kapilar now walking along a narrow path, cloak wrapped tight, as the terraced slopes and forests of Parambu open before him.

dialogue.text: Among the hills of Parambu, he found the Velir chieftain Vel Pari, whose name the poems bind to reckless generosity.

i18n.hi: परंबु की पहाड़ियों में उन्हें वेलिर सरदार वेल पारी मिले, जिनका नाम कविताओं ने बेपरवाह उदारता से बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: heroic medium shot of Vel Pari offering his chariot to a climber-plant while Kapilar watches
panels.action: In a courtyard overlooking steep slopes, Vel Pari, sturdy and open-faced, unhooks a fine chariot and gestures for servants to leave it under a fragile climbing plant, while Kapilar watches, half-smiling at the famous gesture.

dialogue.text: Later retellings tell how Pari gave even his chariot to a creeping plant. The poems praise such open-handedness, where wealth flows like mountain rain.

i18n.hi: बाद की कथाएँ कहती हैं, पारी ने लता के लिए रथ तक दे डाला; गीत उनकी ऐसी खुली हथेली की जय बोलते हैं, जहाँ धन पहाड़ी बारिश सा बहता है।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Kapilar and Pari seated together in a verandah, scrolls and gifts between them
panels.action: Kapilar and Vel Pari sit facing each other on a pillared verandah; between them lie garlands, a sword with jeweled hilt, and a bundle of palm leaves, as attendants move discreetly in the background.

dialogue.speaker: Vel Pari
dialogue.text: Stay, Kapilar. Let your tongue be our drum.

i18n.hi: ठहरो, कापिलर। तुम्हारी ज़बान ही हमारा नगाड़ा बने।

panels.shot: wide shot of Parambu’s stronghold with hills, watchfires, and distant rival banners
panels.action: A wide view shows Pari’s hill-fort, its stone walls clinging to crags; watchfires burn on peaks while, far below, small clusters of rival banners gather at the foothills like creeping storm clouds.

dialogue.text: But Parambu was a hill caught between crowns. The three great lineages watched its passes and its stubborn host.

i18n.hi: परंबु एक पहाड़ी थी, दो–तीन मुकुटों के बीच फँसी; तीनों वंश उसकी दर्रों और उसकी जिद्दी सेना पर नज़र रखे थे।

panels.shot: bird's-eye over three separate royal camps encircling the hills, trails of smoke rising
panels.action: An overhead view reveals three distinct royal camps around the base of the hills—each with its own style of tents and standards—encircling the highlands where Pari’s fort stands aloof, smoke rising from both camps and fortress.

dialogue.text: Purananuru poems remember the three crowned kings turning their gaze on Parambu, a net of siege tightening around a hill of gifts.

i18n.hi: पुराननूरु याद रखता है, कैसे तीनों मुकुटधारी राजा परंबु पर नज़र गड़ाकर घेरा कसते गए, दान की पहाड़ी को जाल में जकड़ते गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kapilar at the edge of a royal camp, facing a group of crowned-kings’ officers
panels.action: Kapilar stands at the edge of a grand camp, dust at his feet, as armored officers of a crowned king stare him down; behind them loom war elephants and lines of spears catching the sun.

dialogue.text: In the songs, Kapilar confronts those powers not with weapons but with verse, asking why kings would hunt a giver rather than honor him.

i18n.hi: गीतों में कापिलर उन ताकतों से हथियार नहीं, शब्दों से भिड़ते हैं, पूछते हैं, राजा दाता का शिकार करेंगे या उसका मान रखेंगे।

panels.shot: close-up on Kapilar’s face, calm but fierce, as he recites toward an unseen ruler
panels.action: A close view shows Kapilar’s lined face, eyes steady, mouth just opening as if mid-verse, with blurred hints of a royal umbrella and throne in the background.

dialogue.speaker: Kapilar
dialogue.text: Will kings claim glory by plundering the hand that feeds strangers?

i18n.hi: क्या राजा उस हाथ को लूटकर कीर्ति कमाएँगे, जो अनजानों को खिलाता है?

panels.shot: wide shot inside a royal pavilion, king listening while warriors look uneasy as Kapilar speaks
panels.action: Inside a great tented pavilion, a crowned ruler sits on a raised seat while Kapilar stands before him; courtiers and warriors glance uneasily at one another as the poet’s raised hand and firm stance command the space.

dialogue.text: The poems do not halt the siege. Yet they hold a mirror to power, binding the three crowns into lines that outlast their campaigns.

i18n.hi: घेराबंदी नहीं रुकती, पर कविताएँ सत्ता को आईना दिखाती हैं, तीनों मुकुटों को ऐसे छंदों में बाँधती हैं जो उनके अभियानों से लंबा जीते हैं।

panels.shot: somber wide shot of Parambu in a later stage of siege, fields empty, watchfires dim
panels.action: Parambu’s slopes look worn: terraced fields lie fallow, cattle are gone, and the watchfires are fewer; Pari stands on the wall, hands on the parapet, as Kapilar watches from the shadows of a tower.

dialogue.text: The siege tightens in the poems’ backdrop. Hunger, delay, and pressure write themselves on stone and bone, though the verses speak more of honor than of detail.

i18n.hi: कविताओं की पृष्ठभूमि में घेरा कसता है; भूख, देर और दबाव पत्थर–हड्डी पर लिखे जाते हैं, पर छंद ज़्यादा इज़्ज़त की बात करते हैं, विवरण की कम।

panels.shot: intense mid-shot of Pari and Kapilar in a dim inner hall, both serious, a lamp between them
panels.action: In a dim inner hall lit by a single lamp, Vel Pari and Kapilar sit facing each other in silence, shadows long; Pari’s hand rests on a spear, Kapilar’s fingers trace invisible letters on the floor.

dialogue.speaker: Vel Pari
dialogue.text: If I fall, let my name live where your words travel.

i18n.hi: अगर मैं गिरूँ, तो मेरा नाम वहीं जिए जहाँ तुम्हारे शब्द पहुँचें।

panels.shot: wide shot showing a battle-scarred hillside after conflict, with broken chariots and empty walls
panels.action: A hillside below Parambu shows abandoned chariots, fallen standards, and trampled earth; the fort’s gate stands open and strangely quiet, with no warriors visible on the walls, only circling birds in the distant sky.

dialogue.text: Later tradition speaks of Pari’s fall under the three crowns. The poems hint at loss, but preserve the man as the peerless giver of Parambu.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा कहती है, तीन मुकुटों के हाथों पारी गिरा; कविताएँ बस क्षति का इशारा करती हैं, पर उसे परंबु का बेजोड़ दाता बनाकर छोड़ती हैं।

panels.shot: gentle indoor medium shot of Kapilar with two young girls, Pari’s daughters, beside a doorway
panels.action: Inside a modest house, Kapilar sits near a doorway with two young girls—Pari’s daughters—standing close to him; he rests a reassuring hand near them while outside a small village bustles.

dialogue.text: Later stories, woven around these poems, place Pari’s daughters in Kapilar’s care, two tender shoots left after a great tree has fallen.

i18n.hi: इन ही गीतों पर बुनी बाद की कथाएँ कहती हैं, पारी की दो बेटियाँ कापिलर की शरण में रहीं, जैसे बड़े पेड़ के गिरने पर दो कोमल टहनियाँ बची रह गई हों।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kapilar at a different court, daughters in the background, addressing another chieftain
panels.action: Kapilar stands respectfully before another chieftain in a new hill court, while the two girls wait behind a pillar; the ruler listens, hand stroking his beard, as attendants watch curiously.

dialogue.speaker: Kapilar
dialogue.text: Honor Pari’s house. Take his daughter as kin, not as burden.

i18n.hi: पारी के घर का मान रखो; उसकी बेटी को बोझ नहीं, अपना खून मानो।

panels.shot: transition shot showing a small map-like view of Parambu and other courts, Kapilar traveling between them
panels.action: A stylized overhead view shows the hills of Parambu and several distant courts connected by faint paths, with a small figure of Kapilar walking those routes, carrying a staff and palm-leaf bundle.

dialogue.text: So the tales remember him: a guardian by verse, going from hall to hall, seeking marriages that would shelter Pari’s line.

i18n.hi: यूँ ही उसे याद रखते हैं: गीतों से पहरा देता संरक्षक, दरबार दरबार घूमते हुए, ऐसे वर खोजता जो पारी की वंशरेखा को आसरा दें।

panels.shot: quiet medium close-up of Kapilar alone under a tree on a rocky hill, lost in thought
panels.action: Kapilar sits alone beneath a gnarled tree on a rocky hillside, staff laid beside him, the distant outline of Parambu barely visible on the horizon as evening light turns the sky amber.

dialogue.text: There are tales of his last act, of ritual death by fasting on the northern stone. Yet the poems themselves are silent; the scholar reads carefully between memory and embellishment.

i18n.hi: एक आख़िरी संकल्प की कथा भी है, उत्तर के पत्थर पर उपवास से प्राण त्याग की; पर खुद कविताएँ चुप हैं, विद्वान स्मृति और सज़ावट के बीच सँभलकर पढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of palm-leaf manuscripts being copied in a later monastery-like setting
panels.action: In a later age, scribes sit in a quiet hall, copying palm-leaf manuscripts by lamplight; a colophon line names Kapilar, while outside, rain falls softly on tiled roofs.

dialogue.text: Colophons remember Kapilar, giver of hill-songs and Pari-poems. Scholars know these attributions are layered, yet through them we hear a voice that set loyalty and generosity into enduring meter.

i18n.hi: टीकाएँ कापिलर को याद रखती हैं, पहाड़ों के गीत और पारी-काव्य के दाता को; विद्वान जानते हैं ये नाम-निशान परतदार हैं, फिर भी इनके पार हमें वही आवाज़ सुनाई देती है जिसने वफ़ादारी और उदारता को स्थायी छंद में ढाल दिया।

panels.shot: final wide shot of modern Parambu hills at dawn, ghostly figures of Kapilar and Pari overlooking
panels.action: The Parambu hills in a modern dawn stretch under soft light, terraced fields and scattered houses visible; faint, translucent figures of Kapilar and Vel Pari stand on a ridge, gazing over the land.

dialogue.text: In these remembered hills, armies have vanished but the poems endure. They tell how, when Parambu fell, a poet’s loyal words guarded its orphaned daughters and tested the conscience of kings.

i18n.hi: इन यादों वाली पहाड़ियों में सेनाएँ गुम हो गईं, पर कविताएँ बचीं; वे बताती हैं, जब परंबु गिरा, तो एक कवि के वफ़ादार शब्दों ने उसकी अनाथ बेटियों की रखवाली की और राजाओं की अंतरात्मा को परखा।

title_i18n.en: The Poet Who Guarded Pari's Daughters
title_i18n.hi: पारी की बेटियों की रखवाली करता कवि

subtitle_i18n.en: Song, Siege, and the Orphaned Hills
